label: Start epidemic
summary: Starts a new epidemic (a spreading disease) in the province.
details: Vanilla always gives both the disease type (for example smallpox, typhus, dysentery) and how strong it is (minor, major or apocalyptic). The new epidemic can be saved under a name so later script can refer to it.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which disease the epidemic is.
fields.values: an epidemic type key, such as smallpox

fields.name: intensity
fields.text: How severe the outbreak is.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new epidemic under this name for later use in the same script.

label: Create faction
summary: Makes the character start a faction of the given type against a target.
details: Vanilla uses it for claimant, peasant and liberty factions, with the target being a liege or another character.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which kind of faction is started.
fields.values: a faction type key, such as claimant_faction

fields.name: target
fields.text: Who the faction is directed against.
fields.values: a character, for example liege or scope:actor.top_liege

label: Create holy order
summary: Founds a new holy order with a leader and a barony as its seat.
details: You can name the order's type directly, or ask for a random one (any, military, monastic or mendicant). Name and coat of arms are optional. The new order can be saved under a name for later use. Vanilla gives the leader, the capital barony and a random type of military.

fields.name: leader
fields.text: The character who leads the order.

fields.name: capital
fields.text: The barony where the order is based.

fields.name: founder
fields.text: The character credited as founder.

fields.name: holy_order_type
fields.text: A specific holy order type.

fields.name: random_holy_order_type
fields.text: Picks a random order type from a group.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The order's name.

fields.name: coat_of_arms
fields.text: The order's coat of arms.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new order under this name.

label: Create holy site
summary: Creates a holy site for the faith in a county or barony.
details: The faith must not already have a holy site of that type, and the chosen barony must not already host another holy site. If the holy site type defines its own location, county and barony are optional and replace that default; otherwise one of them is required. The input shows no vanilla use.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which holy site type to create.
fields.values: a holy site type key or a holy site object

fields.name: eminent
fields.text: Whether the site is an eminent one.

fields.name: county
fields.text: The county the site is in.

fields.name: barony
fields.text: The barony that hosts the site.

fields.name: actor
fields.text: A character the resulting on_action is credited to.

label: Create hybrid culture
summary: Creates a new culture by mixing the character's culture with another culture.
details: The new culture gets a random mix of pillars and traditions from both, the same way the AI hybridizes. It is saved as scope:new_culture. The other culture is written as the value. The game's documentation says the side-effects version is the one that also charges the cost and converts people.

label: Hybridize culture (full)
summary: Creates a hybrid of the character's culture and another one, exactly as if the player had hybridized through the interface.
details: It also charges the cost and does the conversion that the interface action does. The new culture is not saved as a scope, because of technical limitations, the game's documentation says. The plain create_hybrid_culture does only the creation.

label: Create inspiration
summary: Gives the character a new inspiration of the given type.
details: The new inspiration is saved as scope:new_inspiration. Written as a block, it can also set the gold cost, replacing the cost defined in the inspiration type. Vanilla mostly uses the short form with a type name such as book_inspiration.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which inspiration type.

fields.name: gold
fields.text: Overrides the type's base cost.

label: Create legend
summary: Creates a new legend owned by the character.
details: The legend has a type, a quality and a chronicle (the story template). Its properties fill the chronicle's slots, and each key must match a property of that chronicle with an object of the right kind. The protagonist defaults to the character. The new legend can be saved under a name.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The kind of legend.
fields.values: such as heroic, holy or legitimizing

fields.name: quality
fields.text: How grand the legend is.

fields.name: chronicle
fields.text: Which chronicle (story template) the legend follows.

fields.name: properties
fields.text: Fills the chronicle's slots with objects.
fields.values: a block of key = object pairs

fields.name: protagonist
fields.text: Who the legend is about.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new legend under this name.

label: Create legend seed
summary: Creates a legend seed owned by the character.
details: The block has the same shape as create_legend: type, quality, chronicle and properties. The game's documentation does not say what a seed is or how it differs from a finished legend. Vanilla uses it often with famed quality and heroic, holy or legitimizing types.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The kind of legend.
fields.values: such as heroic, holy or legitimizing

fields.name: quality
fields.text: How grand the legend is.

fields.name: chronicle
fields.text: Which chronicle (story template) it follows.

fields.name: properties
fields.text: Fills the chronicle's slots with objects.
fields.values: a block of key = object pairs

label: Create men-at-arms
summary: Creates a men-at-arms regiment for the ruler.
details: If a title is given, the regiment is created as that title's troops. Either name the type or copy the type from an existing regiment, not both. Vanilla nearly always sets check_can_recruit = no; going by its name, that skips the recruiting check, but the game's documentation does not say. A bare type name also works as a short form.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The men-at-arms type.
fields.values: a men-at-arms type key, such as light_footmen

fields.name: type_of
fields.text: Takes the type from an existing regiment. Cannot be combined with type.

fields.name: check_can_recruit
fields.text: Going by its name, whether the game checks that the ruler can recruit this; the game's documentation does not explain it.

fields.name: title
fields.text: Makes it title troops of this title.

fields.name: size
fields.text: The size of the new regiment; the game's documentation gives no unit.

label: Create nomad title
summary: Creates a new title for a nomad and gives it to a holder.
details: The government defaults to nomad, and it must be one that uses county fertility. The optional article, pre and adj take further name texts; if left out, the name is used. The game's documentation does not say what each is for. Vanilla always sets name, holder, government and a saved name for the new title.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The title's name.
fields.values: a localization key or dynamic description

fields.name: holder
fields.text: The character who holds the new title.

fields.name: government
fields.text: The government the title uses.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new title under this name.

fields.name: article
fields.text: An optional extra name text; the game's documentation does not say its role.

fields.name: pre
fields.text: An optional extra name text; the game's documentation does not say its role.

fields.name: adj
fields.text: An optional extra name text; the game's documentation does not say its role.

label: Create rite
summary: Creates a new rite in the character's faith, with the character as its founder.
details: The faith and the founder are used to generate the rite's icon and names. The founder converts to the rite only if convert is yes; it defaults to no. The new rite can be saved under a name.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which rite type to create from.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new rite under this name.

fields.name: convert
fields.text: Whether the founder converts to the new rite.

label: Start story
summary: Starts a story cycle with the character as its owner.
details: It can be written as just the story type name, or as a block that also saves the new story under a name for later use. Vanilla uses types such as story_conqueror and story_cycle_murders_at_court.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which story type.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new story under this name.

label: Create task contract
summary: Creates a task contract of a given type and tier at a location.
details: Type, tier and location are required. An employer, a destination and a target character are optional. The game's documentation spells the tier field task_task_contract_tier, but all 181 vanilla uses write task_contract_tier. The new contract can be saved under a name.

fields.name: task_contract_type
fields.text: Which kind of contract.

fields.name: task_contract_tier
fields.text: The contract's tier.

fields.name: location
fields.text: The province where the contract is.

fields.name: task_contract_employer
fields.text: The employer of the contract.

fields.name: destination
fields.text: A destination province.

fields.name: target
fields.text: A target character for the contract.

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the new contract under this name.

label: Start title change
summary: Starts a batch of title and vassal changes and saves it under a name.
details: You then add single moves (for example change_title_holder) inside that saved change, and finish with resolve_title_and_vassal_change to apply them together. The type decides which on_actions fire, how vassals and the title treasury are handled, and more; for example usurped makes lower-tier vassals independent. The game's documentation text in the input is cut off, so not every type is described here. Vanilla uses types such as granted, created, conquest, independency and swear_fealty.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The kind of title change.
fields.values: a change type such as granted, created, conquest or usurped

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: The name the change is saved under.
fields.values: a name you choose, for example change

fields.name: add_claim_on_loss
fields.text: Whether the old holder gets a weak claim on titles they lose.

label: Custom description
summary: Runs the effects inside it but shows your own text in the tooltip instead of the automatic description.
details: The text is a localization key. Subject defaults to the current scope; object and value are optional and can be used by the text. The effects inside still run as normal.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The localization key shown in place of the automatic description.

fields.name: subject
fields.text: The thing the text is about.

fields.name: object
fields.text: A second thing the text can refer to.

fields.name: value
fields.text: A number the text can show.

label: Custom description, no bullet
summary: Like custom_description, runs its effects but shows your own text, and leaves out the bullet point.
details: It takes the same text, subject, object and value as custom_description. Vanilla uses it 532 times, nearly always with just a text key.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The localization key shown in place of the automatic description.

fields.name: subject
fields.text: The thing the text is about.

fields.name: object
fields.text: A second thing the text can refer to.

fields.name: value
fields.text: A number the text can show.

label: Custom label
summary: Shows a tooltip line from a localization key, used for grouping and wording.
details: The game's documentation says the scope is used as the object. It can also be written as a block with text, an optional subject and hidden effects. The game's documentation is terse, so how it differs from custom_tooltip is not stated.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The localization key to show.

fields.name: subject
fields.text: The thing the text is about.

label: Custom tooltip
summary: Shows a text line in the tooltip; the text itself changes nothing in the game.
details: The game's documentation says the current scope is the subject, used for grouping and wording. Written as a block it takes text, an optional subject and effects, which are hidden. Vanilla uses it in very many places, mostly as a plain key.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The localization key to show.

fields.name: subject
fields.text: The thing the text is about.

label: Die
summary: Kills the character.
details: Give a death reason and optionally a killer. An artifact can be named as the murder weapon, replacing the default one from the killer's slot for that death reason. Writing death = natural picks a natural cause of death instead.

fields.name: death_reason
fields.text: How the character dies.
fields.values: a death reason key, such as death_execution

fields.name: killer
fields.text: Who killed them.

fields.name: artifact
fields.text: The artifact used to kill, instead of the default one.

label: Create organization (debug)
summary: A debug effect on a character; the game documents it only as TODO.

label: Debug log
summary: Writes a message to the debug log when it runs.
details: The message can be a localization string, which can use ROOT, SCOPE and PREV.

label: Log date
summary: Writes the current date to the debug log.
details: Vanilla always writes it as yes.

label: Log scopes
summary: Writes the current scope to the debug log.
details: With yes it writes full scope information, with no only the current scope.

label: Log with stack trace
summary: Writes a message followed by a stack trace to the debug log.
details: The message can be a localization string, which can use ROOT, SCOPE and PREV. The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Trigger event (debug)
summary: Triggers an event like trigger_event, and also prints the event's trigger check and immediate effects.
details: The game's documentation gives no usage line, so the exact way to write it is not shown. The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Decline activity invite
summary: Makes the character decline their invitation to the given activity.

label: Delay journey
summary: Pauses the travel plan for a length of time, then lets it continue.
details: The delay is added to any delay already running, unless add = no is set. Write the length in days, weeks, months or years. Vanilla mostly uses days.

fields.name: days
fields.text: Delay in days.

fields.name: weeks
fields.text: Delay in weeks.

fields.name: months
fields.text: Delay in months.

fields.name: years
fields.text: Delay in years.

fields.name: add
fields.text: Whether to add to an existing delay or replace it.

label: Reduce army
summary: Kills a share of the army's current soldiers.
details: The value is the share that dies, as a fraction: 0.2 means a fifth. Vanilla uses numbers like 0.1, 0.4 and 0.9, and once a script value.

label: Depose
summary: Deposes the character.
details: The game's documentation says nothing more about what being deposed does. Vanilla always writes depose = yes.

label: Depose diarch
summary: Removes the character's current diarch and replaces them with the next in the line of succession.
details: Written as yes or no; vanilla always writes yes. The game's documentation does not say more about what a diarch is.

label: Designate diarch
summary: Names the target character as a future diarch of the character.
details: It marks them as designated; the game's documentation does not say when they take over. Vanilla gives the target as a character, a title's holder or a saved scope.

label: Destroy event troops
summary: Destroys all event troop regiments that belong to the character.
details: The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Destroy artifact
summary: Destroys the given artifact, whoever owns it.
details: destroy_owned_artifact is described as the safer version of this.

label: Destroy memory
summary: Destroys the given character memory.
details: The memory is removed, so do not use that saved scope after this runs.

label: Destroy faction
summary: Destroys the faction.
details: Vanilla always writes destroy_faction = yes.

label: Destroy inspiration
summary: Destroys the given inspiration.
details: The inspiration is removed, so do not use that saved scope after this runs.

label: Disband regiment
summary: Destroys the men-at-arms regiment.
details: It does not work on regiments that belong to mercenary companies or holy orders. Vanilla always writes destroy_maa_regiment = yes.

label: Destroy owned artifact
summary: Destroys an artifact that the character owns.
details: The game's documentation calls it a safer version of destroy_artifact; it does not say what exactly makes it safer. The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Destroy title
summary: Destroys the given title.
details: Vanilla gives the title as prev, a saved scope or a title link. The game's documentation says nothing about what happens to its holder or vassals.
